package_info.package_versions: Multiple versions affected by zero-day vulnerabilities (exact versions not specified in report)
package_info.why_malicious: The Struts2 package contained critical vulnerabilities in its core request handling logic, specifically in the OGNL expression evaluation and multipart parser, which allowed attackers to inject and execute arbitrary system commands via crafted HTTP requests. This enabled remote code execution (RCE) and led to the compromise of web applications, as seen in the Equifax breach where 143 million consumer records were stolen.

execution_context.trigger: During HTTP request processing (at runtime, when handling inbound web requests)
execution_context.file_location: Core Struts2 request handling classes, specifically the Jakarta Multipart parser and OGNL expression evaluation logic (e.g., org.apache.struts2.dispatcher.multipart.JakartaMultiPartRequest, org.apache.struts2.views.jsp.StrutsBodyTagSupport)
required_permissions: network (to receive HTTP requests and send responses)
filesystem (to read/write files as part of command execution)
process execution (to spawn system commands via Runtime.exec)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
Attacker-supplied HTTP request with malicious OGNL expression, e.g.:
Content-Type: %{(#_='multipart/form-data').
(#dm=@ognl.OgnlContext@DEFAULT_MEMBER_ACCESS).
(#_memberAccess?((#_memberAccess=#dm)):((#container=#context['com.opensymphony.xwork2.ActionContext.container']).
(#ognlUtil=#container.getInstance(@com.opensymphony.xwork2.ognl.OgnlUtil@class)).
(#ognlUtil.getExcludedPackageNames().clear()).
(#ognlUtil.getExcludedClasses().clear()).
(#context.setMemberAccess(#dm)))).
(@java.lang.Runtime@getRuntime().exec('id'))}
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During HTTP request processing, the code evaluates attacker-supplied OGNL expressions embedded in HTTP headers, disables OGNL security restrictions, executes arbitrary system commands on the server, and enables exfiltration or manipulation of sensitive data.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code evaluates user-supplied OGNL expressions in a privileged context, allowing attackers to bypass security controls and execute arbitrary system commands on the server. This is a textbook example of remote code execution vulnerability.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normally, HTTP headers and parameters are treated as untrusted data and never executed as code. The actual behavior allows untrusted input to be parsed and executed as OGNL expressions, violating the principle of input validation and code/data separation.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: OGNL is legitimately used in Struts2 for safe data binding and expression evaluation within templates, but it should never evaluate untrusted user input or allow modification of the security context.
key_indicators: OGNL expression evaluation on untrusted HTTP headers or parameters
Modification of OGNL member access or security context (e.g., setting #_memberAccess or clearing excluded classes/packages)
Invocation of system-level commands via Runtime.getRuntime().exec
Absence of input sanitization or validation before OGNL evaluation
Unexpected Content-Type or parameter values containing OGNL syntax

attack_chain.action: Attacker sends a specially crafted HTTP request containing a malicious OGNL expression in the Content-Type header or request parameters.
attack_chain.leads_to: The Struts2 framework parses the request and evaluates the OGNL expression.

attack_chain.action: The OGNL expression disables security restrictions and executes arbitrary system commands on the server.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains remote code execution privileges on the server.

attack_chain.action: Attacker leverages remote code execution to access and exfiltrate sensitive data, such as consumer records.
attack_chain.leads_to: Data breach and loss of customer data from the compromised application.

behavioral_signatures: OGNL expression evaluation triggered by untrusted HTTP headers or parameters
Runtime execution of system commands (e.g., Runtime.getRuntime().exec) initiated during web request processing
Modification of OGNL member access or clearing of excluded classes/packages at runtime
Unexpected changes to the security context within OGNL evaluation
file_indicators: References to org.apache.struts2.dispatcher.multipart.JakartaMultiPartRequest or related multipart parsing classes
Modifications to struts.xml or configuration files enabling custom OGNL evaluation or altering security settings
Presence of custom or unexpected OGNL expressions in application logs
network_indicators: Inbound HTTP requests with Content-Type or parameters containing OGNL syntax (e.g., %{...})
Unusual HTTP requests with multipart/form-data and embedded OGNL payloads
Outbound connections or data exfiltration attempts following suspicious web requests
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor web application logs for OGNL expressions in HTTP headers or parameters, especially those attempting to modify member access or execute system commands. Deploy web application firewalls (WAFs) with rules to block or alert on OGNL payload patterns. Audit for unexpected process execution by the web server user. Regularly scan for and patch vulnerable Struts2 versions. Review configuration files for unauthorized changes to OGNL or security settings.
